newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's LUKoil still in Caspian deal with Azeris.
newsitem.headline: Russia's LUKoil still in Caspian deal with Azeris.

text.p: Russia's LUKoil said on Friday it still plans to develop a disputed Caspian oil deposit with Azerbaijan despite the likely withdrawal of the third partner in the deal, Russia's state oil firm Rosneft.
LUKoil spokesman Pyotr Neyev said it was too early to say whether LUKoil would bid for Rosneft's share in the agreement or whether another partner would be brought in.
"LUKoil is still in the project at this moment," Neyev said.

"I cannot exclude the possibility that LUKoil will hold talks with Azerbaijan, and it's too early to say whether LUKoil will bid for that (Rosneft's) part of the project. We also cannot exclude a new third party being involved."
LUKoil and Rosneft signed a deal on July 4 to develop the field with Azerbaijan's state oil company SOCAR. The deposit is estimated to contain over 50 million tonnes of oil reserves.
Under the deal, which was only a preliminary one, SOCAR was to get 50 percent of the project, LUKoil 30 percent and Rosneft 20 percent.
The deal caused consternation on the part of Turkmenistan, which also lays claim to the field, which it calls Serdar.
The project has reopened old wounds between littoral Caspian states which have yet to agree on how to divide up the resource-rich territory.
Turkmen leader Saparmurat Niyazov is expected to discuss the status of the field and the Caspian in general with Russian President Bori Yeltsin when he visits Moscow on August 7.
Rosneft told Interfax news agency late on Thursday that it was withdrawing from the $1 billion project, although there is still some confusion over the announcement.

Vladimir Vyunitsky, a Rosneft spokesman loyal to company president Yuri Bespalov, told Reuters on Friday that a decision was taken to withdraw from the project to develop the field, called Kyapaz by the Azeris.

But Vladimir Tumarkin, who has officially resigned with other top officials over differences with Bespalov but who is still working at Rosneft, said Thursday's decision to withdraw from Kyapaz was not final.
"It is too early to say finally that we have left the project," Tumarkin said.

"There was a meeting of company management under the direction of Bespalov, and they decided to recommend that Rosneft should withdraw from Kyapaz. But this was done without the participation of Putilov," he added.

Alexander Putilov is chairman of the board at Rosneft and does not see eye to eye with Bespalov on the future of the company. Infighting has intensified as the privatisation of the last fully state-owned oil company in Russia approaches.
A 51 percent stake in the company is due to go under the hammer in September.

Tumarkin said the decision to recommend withdrawing from the Caspian project was connected with the territorial dispute between Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan. Vyunitksy also said the decision was based on the uneconomic conditions of the deal.

Vyunitsky said Rosneft's Bespalov was preparing to visit Baku and Ashgabat to discuss future cooperation in the Caspian region. Meanwhile, LUKoil would continue to work in the region notwithstanding territorial disputes.
"LUKoil will not stop with this project, but will work further with Azerbaijan if it in the interests of our company," LUKoil's Neyev said.
--Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +709 941 8520
